He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]]. ==College career== Black, raised in [[Concord, North Carolina]], committed to coach [[Roy Williams (basketball coach)|Roy Williams]] and North Carolina as a high school sophomore.{{cite web|title=Leaky Black Commits to UNC|url=https://www.tarheeltimes.com/article72257.aspx|website=TarHeelTimes.com|date=January 15, 2016|access-date=March 22, 2024}} After a shortened freshman campaign due to an ankle injury, Black entered the starting lineup in his sophomore season for the Tar Heels.{{cite news|first=Billy|last=Witz|title=Leaky Black Has a Lot on His Mind, And That's OK|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/04/03/sports/ncaabasketball/leaky-black-unc.html|work=[[New York Times]]|date=April 3, 2022|access-date=April 4, 2022}} As a senior, Black became one of the top defensive players in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]], earning conference all-defensive team honors at the close of the regular season.{{cite news|first=Michael|last=Koh|title=Armando Bacot Named First Team All-ACC, Leaky Black Named to All-Defensive Team|url=https://chapelboro.com/sports/armando-bacot-named-first-team-all-acc-leaky-black-named-to-all-defensive-team|work=[[Chapelboro]]|date=March 7, 2022|access-date=April 4, 2022}} Black was a part of a Tar Heel starting lineup that each averaged big minutes and led the eighth-seeded Tar Heels to an unexpected Final Four berth in the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2022 NCAA tournament]].{{Cite web |title=2021-22 UNC Tar Heels Men's Roster and Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/north-carolina/men/2022.html |access-date=2025-05-31 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}} In the semifinal against rival [[2021–22 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]], Black held Duke freshman [[AJ Griffin (basketball)|AJ Griffin]] to 1–7 shooting for 6 points to help secure the win.{{cite news|first=Adam|last=Smith|title=Final Four run provides connecting point in leadership growth for UNC senior Leaky Black|url=https://www.thetimesnews.com/story/sports/college/acc/2022/03/31/unc-basketball-leaky-blacks-role-grows-way-final-four-vs-duke-ncaa-tournament/7226488001/|work=[[Times-News (Burlington, North Carolina)|Times-News]]|date=March 31, 2022|access-date=April 4, 2022}}{{cite magazine|first=Kevin|last=Sweeney|title=Five Matchups That Will Decide UNC-Kansas Title Game|url=https://www.si.com/college/2022/04/03/five-matchups-decide-unc-kansas-title-game|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=April 3, 2022|access-date=April 4, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Charlotte Hornets / Greensboro Swarm (2023–2024)=== After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Black signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Charlotte Hornets]] on July 19, 2023.{{cite web|first=Sam|last=Perley|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Leaky Black To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-sign-leaky-black-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 19, 2023|access-date=July 20, 2023}} He made 26 appearances (including three starts) for Charlotte during his rookie season, recording averages of 2.7 points, 1.5 rebounds, and 1.8 assists.{{Cite web|title=Leaky Black 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4395650/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} However, Black was waived by the Hornets on August 1, 2024.{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Waive Leaky Black|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-waive-leaky-black|website=NBA.com|date=August 1, 2024|access-date=August 1, 2024}} === Washington Wizards / Capital City Go-Go (2024–2026)=== On September 29, 2024, Black signed with the [[Washington Wizards]],{{cite web|title=Wizards Announce 2024 Training Camp Roster/Schedule|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-announce-2024-training-camp-roster-schedule|website=NBA.com|date=September 29, 2024|access-date=September 30, 2024}} but was waived on October 12.{{cite tweet|author=Wizards PR|title=Official: The Washington Wizards have waived G Kira Lewis Jr. and F Leaky Black.|number=1845129032238608612|user=WizPRStats|date=October 12, 2024|access-date=October 13, 2024}} On October 28, he joined the [[Capital City Go-Go]].{{cite web|title=Go-Go Announce Training Camp Roster, Dates|url=https://capitalcity.gleague.nba.com/news/go-go-announce-training-camp-roster-dates-2|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}} On October 2, 2025, the Wizards added Black to their training camp roster, prior to the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]].{{cite web | title=Wizards' Leaky Black: Signs Exhibit 10 deal with Wizards | website=CBS Sports | date=2025-10-02 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/wizards-leaky-black-signs-exhibit-10-deal-with-wizards/ | access-date=2025-12-01}} Black was later released and then re-added to the Go-Go's roster. On February 21, 2026, the Wizards signed Black to a two-way contract.{{Cite web|title=Wizards' Leaky Black: Gets two-way deal with Washington|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/wizards-leaky-black-gets-two-way-deal-with-washington/|access-date=February 23, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} He made 15 appearances (nine starts) for Washington over the remainder of the year, averaging career-highs in points (7.1), rebounds (5.0), assists (1.5), and steals (1.2).{{Cite web|title=Leaky Black 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4395650/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}}
